detail.longDescription: Hey there...! Awkward silence Okay, I’m not famous yet... Umm... Well. How are you guys doing? Did you eat your lentils? I didn’t, I think they’re gross. Anyway, today I’m writing this unprofessional, attitude-filled abomination of a post to talk about .Coma, the bilingual ES/EN programming language that goes from Nim to LLVM (native binary) and is capable of competing against C (a knife fight to the death xd). And yes, I’m only 14 years old—so I’m definitely going to flex that and I don’t care what anyone says :). Alright, enough jokes. Why did I create .Coma? I created .Coma because I felt decent programming languages are unnecessarily complicated—why not translate a script simpler than a Python script down to low level? Without the famous Garbage Collector, simple, human, and readable. Why is it called .Coma? I chose the name .Coma because on day one it sounded so bad I wanted it, and then I found tons of meanings—initially it was just Coma, and I added that `.` because it’s like C++ or C#, a joke about the C family’s need to tack a weird symbol onto the end, except instead of at the end it’s at the start. Plus, "Coma" in Spanish is literally "," which with the `.` sounds like `;`, which is the exact thing that doesn’t exist in this language, along with other weird symbols. My motivations? I want to build something bigger in the future, make systems so good—first to show off :), second, to create a wide range of compatibility and a friendly network for everyone; I want to do this because I like it and I want to change the world, that’s my motivation. What's my goal here? I want you to clone this GitHub repo, tear it apart, and humble my ego until I can't even get out of bed. Why? So I can fix it. I want you to criticize everything and break all my code—just send it my way, and I'll fix it. Anyway, here are the links: - GitHub: https://github.com/Agm1ne/.Coma - Product Hunt: https://www.producthunt.com/products/coma-2?launch=coma-2 And with that I’m signing off. Bye-bye!
